[[Tbilisi]], [[Georgia (country)|Georgia]]| capacity = 2,000| chairman = [[Guram Rukhadze]] | manager = Aleksandre Intskirveli | league = [[Liga 3 (Georgia)]] | season = 2025 | position = 6th of 16 | pattern_la1=_erreadiamantis21ggw|pattern_b1=_erreadiamantis21ggw|pattern_ra1=_erreadiamantis21ggw|pattern_sh1=| leftarm1=008800|body1=008800|rightarm1=008800|shorts1=008800|socks1=008800| pattern_la2=_thinwhiteborder|pattern_b2=_witgeorgia19a|pattern_ra2=_thinwhiteborder | leftarm2=000000|body2=000000|rightarm2=000000|shorts2=000000|socks2=000000| pattern_la3=|pattern_b3=_witgeorgia19t|pattern_ra3= | leftarm3=ffffff|body3=ffffff|rightarm3=ffffff|shorts3=ffffff|socks3=ffffff| }} '''FC WIT Georgia''' is a [[Georgia (country)|Georgian]] [[association football|football]] team from [[Tbilisi]]. The team is sponsored by WIT Georgia Ltd (a subsidiary of the United States WIT, Inc.), a pet food, accessories, and human and veterinary pharmaceuticals import company. WIT stands for World Innovation Technologies. They play their home games at [[Mikheil Meskhi Stadium]] in Tbilisi. In 2004, FC WIT Georgia won the Georgian Championship, qualifying them for the early stages of the [[2004–05 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]. In 2009, they won the championship for the second time.{{cite web|title=Season review: Georgia|url=http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=geo/news/newsid=836972.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104033912/http://www.uefa.com/memberassociations/association=geo/news/newsid=836972.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 4, 2012|publisher=UEFA|access-date=16 September 2011|date=9 June 2009}} In 2010, the team won the [[Georgian Cup]] for the first time.{{cite web|title=WIT claim maiden Georgian Cup triumph|url=https://www.uefa.com/news-media/news/01e5-0f85f312976e-25b1dae8b01b-1000--wit-claim-maiden-georgian-cup-triumph/|publisher=UEFA|access-date=16 September 2011|date=26 May 2010}} However, performance of WIT Georgia was faded after 2010–11 season and relegated to [[Pirveli Liga]] in 2014–15 season. In 2017–18, they finished second in the [[Erovnuli Liga 2]] and secured promotion to the Erovnuli Liga."}}
